results.title: Recursive binary search
results.expected_rationale: Each recursive call halves [low, high], so the worst-case number of calls is logarithmic.
results.explanation: Recognized T(n) = T(n / 2) + O(1) and applied master_theorem_case_2a, yielding O(log n). This is a heuristic syntax match under the listed recurrence assumptions. Other helper calls, library costs, and complex control flow are not analyzed; this is not a proof.

recurrence_evidence.base_case: recognized terminating base case required by the language-specific matcher
assumptions: The selected method has one mutually exclusive recursive branch per call.
The midpoint divides the inclusive [low, high] interval into halves.
The bounds are valid array indices and array access is O(1).
The base case returns when low > high.

results.title: Memoized Fibonacci
results.expected_rationale: Memoization computes each distinct argument once, with average O(1) cache access; this uses the approved usual DSA unit-cost arithmetic model.
results.explanation: Recognized O(1) work for each of at most n + 1 distinct cached states and applied memoized_monotone_scalar_states, yielding O(n). This is a heuristic syntax match under the listed recurrence assumptions. Called helper functions are not included; this estimate is not a proof.

recurrence_evidence.recursive_call_pattern: cached direct self-calls with strictly decreasing scalar state
recurrence_evidence.recurrence: O(1) work for each of at most n + 1 distinct cached states
assumptions: The scalar parameter is a non-negative integer bounded by n.
An unbounded cache stores each argument state once with average O(1) access.
Every recursive argument decreases by a positive constant and reaches the base case.
No input-sized loop or hidden helper work occurs in the function.

results.title: Quicksort with last-element pivot
results.expected_rationale: Sorted or all-equal input makes each partition maximally unbalanced, summing n + (n-1) + ... + 1 comparisons/work.
results.explanation: Recognized T(n) = T(n - 1) + O(n) and applied worst_case_decrement_recurrence_linear_work, yielding O(n^2). This is a heuristic syntax match under the listed recurrence assumptions. Other helper calls, library costs, and complex control flow are not analyzed; this is not a proof.

recurrence_evidence.base_case: recognized terminating base case required by the language-specific matcher
assumptions: The recursive method partitions around the last array element.
Some sorted or all-equal inputs can place the pivot at an endpoint.
Partition scans the current range once and performs O(n) work.
Worst-case time is requested; the smaller recursive subproblem may be empty.
The second recursive call on an empty subproblem has constant work.
